1: # unowa: progress, lessons and handoff
2: 
3: Status date: 2026-11-22. This document distils 25 commits (`ffbb45b..cdbb933`),
4: the uncommitted field-map work in the working tree, `docs/status.md`,
5: `UNOWA.md`, `UNOWA-2.md`, `docs/reuse-audit.md`, `docs/eidos-review.md`,
6: `docs/frame25-crash.md`, and the transcripts in `docs/transcripts/`.
7: 
8: Status vocabulary is the one `docs/status.md` uses: implemented / compiled /
9: tested headlessly / tested in emulator / verified on Old 3DS. Nothing in this
10: project has reached the last one.
11: 
12: ## 0. The short version
13: 
14: - The port boots the original game, renders the Game Freak/Pokémon/Nintendo
15:   logos, the copyright screen, the whole intro movie, the Pokémon Black title,
16:   the start menu, the new-game intro, name entry, and the first field map
17:   (Nuvema Town) in 3D.
18: - M0, M1 and M2 are complete for their exit criteria. M3 is substantially
19:   working. M4 and M5 are in progress. M6 (widescreen), M7 (optimization),
20:   M8 (coverage) and M9 (packaging) have not started.
21: - The architectural unknowns are mostly resolved. The remaining work is
22:   breadth (all the game's scenes and systems), correctness (display capture,
23:   VRAM banking, shading), performance on real hardware, and packaging.
24: - The port is not close to shippable. There is no physical Old 3DS in this
25:   environment, so the 30 FPS target, audio cost, memory headroom and thermal
26:   behaviour are all unmeasured. LOTUS is an integration debugger, not a timing
27:   authority.
28: - The two biggest technical risks are the heuristic flat-image generator and
29:   the source-rewriting layer that feeds it. Both work, but both encode many
30:   special cases and will be expensive to maintain. The principled replacement
31:   (Aletheia's own data companions) is now unblocked but not adopted.
32: - The two biggest handoff risks are machine-local dependencies (sibling
33:   checkouts, generated sinjoh libraries, ROM extract, LOTUS host config and
34:   content pack) and the uncommitted field-map work in the working tree.
35: 
36: ---
37: 
38: ## 1. What unowa is
39: 
40: unowa is a native ARM11 port of Pokémon Black and White for the original
41: Nintendo 3DS / 2DS. It is not an NDS emulator. The game logic is Aletheia's
42: reconstructed Gen V source, compiled for ARM11 with devkitARM. The DS hardware
43: is modelled by compatibility code and rendered through the PICA200. The
44: platform skeleton, DS memory model, 2D/3D renderer, audio output and content
45: pack reader come from sinjoh, itself adapted from kohjoh. Coffeepot is the
46: hardware and engineering reference. Eidos is a design reference only; it is not
47: a build dependency.
48: 
49: Target experience, from `UNOWA.md`: 30 FPS on stock Old 3DS, 400×240 top and
50: 320×240 bottom, widened 3D view, GPU-native 2D, WideArt, original mechanics,
51: both editions, `.3dsx`/CIA packaging, user-supplied ROM data. Initial
52: exclusions: stereo 3D, 60 FPS interpolation, software rendering, xBRZ, live
53: WideArt generation, New 3DS-only optimizations, and a self-contained
54: ROM-containing CIA.
55: 
56: Current build artifacts:
57: 
58: - `build/game/3ds/m1-test.3dsx` — about 5.3 MiB, the game build.
59: - `build/game/3ds/m1-test.elf` — about 52 MiB, unstripped debug ELF.
60: - `build/black/3ds/unowa-black.3dsx`, `build/black/3ds-prof/unowa-black-dbg.3dsx`,
61:   and the White equivalents — the four M0 bootstrap builds (150052 / 150332
62:   bytes each).
63: 
64: The game build is Black only. The White ROM is verified and pinned, but there
65: is no White content pack and no White game build/test yet.
66: 
67: ---
68: 
69: ## 2. Roadmap status
70: 
71: The milestone table in `docs/status.md` lags the detailed evidence below it.
72: This is the corrected reading.
73: 
74: | Milestone | State | What exists | What is missing |
75: |---|---|---|---|
76: | **M0 — Bootstrap** | Complete. Implemented, compiled, tested in emulator. | Four `.3dsx` (Black/White × release/profile), separate object trees, build locks, async SD log, 30 Hz clear presentation, ABI assertions, pinned toolchain. | Nothing for M0. The clear path is deliberately not the game renderer. |
77: | **M1 — Game compilation** | Complete. Implemented, compiled, linked, tested headlessly and in emulator. | Aletheia `src/game` closure: 1,196 objects, 58 MiB archive. Gen V/Gen IV and MSL/newlib symbol collisions resolved by `objcopy --redefine-sym`. Metrowerks asm, MSL runtime, BIOS SVCs and fixed-address symbols replaced in C. `link-final` produces a bootable `.3dsx`. | White game build/pack; authoritative data companions instead of the heuristic generator. |
78: | **M2 — Native boot** | Complete in practice, emulator only. | Game's own `NitroMain` loop runs one tick per DS V-blank (60 Hz). 15–18 overlays load at runtime. DS firmware state, shared work area, PM, PXI, NVRAM, save device, input, V-blank pacing and unsupported-service logging work. The title and intro execute original code. | Host32/3DS checkpoint agreement was never built. Hardware verification. The table still says "in progress"; the exit criterion is met. |
79: | **M3 — 2D** | Substantially complete, not formally closed. | sinjoh's `g2d.c`, `atlas.c`, `pica/gpu.c`, `pica/targets.c` adapted. Text, affine, extended and direct-colour BGs; 4bpp/8bpp tiles; OBJ; windows; alpha blending; BLDY/master brightness; mosaic state; per-line HBlank shadow; VRAMCNT decode. Logos, copyright, full intro movie, title, start menu, name-entry keyboard. | 256-colour bitmap BGs remain unsupported. WideArt side bands are a stub. Some effects/edge cases are unvalidated. The intro's vertical striping is unresolved (may be the game's film-strip motif). No full oracle corpus. |
80: | **M4 — 3D** | In progress; major slice working. | `kj_g3.c`, `g3d.c`, `textures.c`, PICA backend imported. GPU-visible geometry storage (`linearAlloc`), geometry swap seam, 3D publishing, title 3D on top, title phase 2 3D on the lower screen via `GX_DISPMODE_VRAM_D`, Nuvema Town field in 3D. | `DISPCAPCNT` is not modelled as a real 256×192 capture with EVA/EVB A+B blend. VRAM bank remapping is approximated by a flat BG VRAM view. Title phase-2 shading is not oracle-verified. Battle/field 3D coverage and culling/retained geometry are not exercised. |
81: | **M5 — Gameplay** | Early in progress. | Title → start menu → NEW GAME → gender/name entry → Professor Juniper intro → Cheren/Bianca intro → first field-map entry. D-pad and touch input; text advancing; save device exists; ARM7 sound clock runs. | Walking/collision/camera interaction, save/continue flow, wild/trainer battles, menus beyond the start menu, audio output (LOTUS still reports zero samples), script coverage, resource loading at scale. The next field stop after Nuvema Town is not yet characterized. |
82: | **M6 — Widescreen** | Not started. | Nothing. The picture is the DS 256×192 composition at 1.25× (320×240), centred at +40 px on the 400 px top screen. | Wider 3D camera/culling; widened 2D logical composition; B/W WideArt corpus; side-band art; touch-region relocation. |
83: | **M7 — Optimization** | Not started. | Instrumentation counters exist (mainloop, V-blanks, presents, g3 frames/verts/batches, per-target draws, direct-BG cells). | Real O3DS profiling; frame-time budgets; memory ledger; audio mixer cost; GPU contention; hot-path removal; target 30 FPS signoff. |
84: | **M8 — Coverage** | Not started. | Ad hoc LOTUS/ melonDS runs only. | Deterministic saves, recorded inputs, scene corpus, regression comparisons, edition/language/season coverage, lifecycle tests. |
85: | **M9 — Packaging** | Not started. | Manual content pack; manual LOTUS asset registration. | Release build flow, CIA forwarders, installer, clean install/cold boot tests, save integrity, documentation, legal/provenance review. |
86: 
87: ### How far along is it, honestly?
88: 
89: By milestone count, four of ten are effectively complete (M0–M3), M4 is more
90: than half done and M5 has begun. That sounds like 50%+. It is not. The milestone
91: list is ordered by dependency, not by effort. M6–M9 contain the long tail:
92: every remaining scene and battle, all of the widescreen art and layout work,
93: all hardware performance work, a full-game regression corpus, and packaging.
94: The current state is a strong vertical slice through the first hours of the
95: game, not a nearly finished port.
96: 
97: A fair one-sentence estimate: **the port is at the M4/M5 boundary — the engine
98: and the first playable slice exist, but the game is not yet broadly playable,
99: and none of the shipping work has started.**
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## 3. What has been accomplished, milestone by milestone
104: 
105: ### M0 — Bootstrap
106: 
107: - Pinned Aletheia `50731dd`, sinjoh `1774be6`, kohjoh `7a98ace`, Eidos
108:   `2319b45`, coffeepot `209c8ed` in `upstream.lock`; toolchain pins are
109:   devkitARM r68-1 / GCC 16.1.0, libctru 2.7.1, citro3d 1.7.1, 3dstools 1.3.1,
110:   picasso, tex3ds.
111: - Four build variants with isolated object trees and a per-tree `mkdir` lock.
112: - Asynchronous SD log, edition identity, path roots, ABI assertions
113:   (`engine/runtime/abi_assert.c`).
114: - The first LOTUS runs captured pure black; the cause was a missing
115:   `C3D_FrameDrawOn` in the clear path. Fixed and re-verified. This was a real
116:   bug, not a harness artefact.
117: - `tools/build.ps1` and `tools/build.sh` build the M0 shell. The M0 shell is
118:   still useful as a toolchain/LOTUS smoke test, but it is not the game build.
119: 
120: ### M1 — Game compilation
121: 
122: - Aletheia's `src/game` is compiled with devkitARM against sinjoh's NitroSDK /
123:   NitroSystem compatibility libraries. The first probe compiled 360 of 411
124:   core TUs; 938 of 981 overlay TUs. Failures are Metrowerks asm, missing
125:   generated `.inc` data, GCC struct-size assertions, or files whose symbols
126:   sinjoh already provides. They are listed with reasons in
127:   `engine/game_blocklist.txt` and `engine/game_overlay_blocklist.txt`.
128: - The final archive holds 1,196 objects (58 MiB). The data image covers 238
129:   modules in 247 spans; the pointer tables hold roughly 7,200 function
130:   pointers and 3,000 flat data pointers.
131: - `tools/rename_genv.py` resolves the Gen V/Gen IV and MSL/newlib collision
132:   problem: it computes collisions with `nm`, rewrites both archives with
133:   `objcopy --redefine-sym`, and keeps the game's own implementation without a
134:   duplicate definition. `--start-group` is required because the archives call
135:   each other.
136: - `engine/stubs/port_stubs.c` supplies what the DS got from linker symbols,
137:   BIOS SVCs or the MSL runtime: fixed-address values, `bw_limit_get`, OV230
138:   call-through stubs, memory helpers, RC4, SHA-1, HMAC-SHA1, the `CPSi_big_*`
139:   limb readers, non-TWL console identity, and DS hardware no-ops.
140: - `engine/stubs/card_backup_port.c` replaces the DS card-bus backup device with
141:   a 512 KiB flash image backed by `sdmc:/3ds/unowa/saves/<edition>.sav`.
142: - `tools/pack_game_data.py` builds a B/W content pack in sinjoh's PLATPAK v1
143:   format from Aletheia's FNT file-ID mapping. The Black pack is 247 files /
144:   198,011,852 bytes, build id `unowa-nitrofs-1`.
145: - `make -f engine/game.mk link-final` produces a real ARM11 ELF and `.3dsx`.
146:   `verify-pins` and `verify-rom` are reproducible checks.
147: 
148: ### M2 — Native boot
149: 
150: The important result is that the game's own loop now runs at 60 Hz, not that
151: the screens are no longer black. The fault chain, in the order it was found:
152: 
153: | Symptom | Root cause | Fix |
154: |---|---|---|
155: | Fault at `0x04004000` in `OS_IsRunOnTwl` | DS SCFG register read | Port returns non-TWL; `OS_GetConsoleType` redirected to `0x80000001`. |
156: | Fault at `0x04004004` in `SCFG_SetCpuSpeed` | `reg_SCFG_CLK` read | Patcher fixup replaces the read with 0. |
157: | Fault at `0x04000208` (`REG_IME`) | Bare DS I/O register access in game source | `tools/gen_port_ioreg_header.py` rewrites all 170 `IOREG_ADDR(...)` macros onto sinjoh's `NitroPort_*` shadow arrays; forced include with the original guard. |
158: | Boot spins in `PMi_WaitBusy` | `NitroPort_InitArm7Services()` never called; PXI FIFO drain gated on real ARM IRQ mode | Call `NitroPort_InitArm7Services()` before `NitroMain`; make the drain unconditional; initialize the Gen V PM state directly (`unowa_pm_ensure_ready`) because sinjoh's `os_init.o` initializes a different PM state. |
159: | Unmapped write at `0x02000008` | `OS_CreateExtraHeap` hardcodes `(Cell *)0x02000000` | Dedicated `unowa_extra_heap[0x4000]`, not `NitroPort_MainMem`, which overlaps the SDK arena at `0x4e1000`. |
160: | Jump to `0x02081e7c` | `MATHi_SHA1ProcessMessageBlockFunc` holds a raw ROM function address | Port defines the pointer to the C transform and excludes it from the data image. |
161: | Jump to `0x02155160` | `_wifiDeviceTable` holds DS Thumb pointers into ov009 | Inert 51-slot stub table in `port_stubs.c`; excluded from the data image. |
162: | Frame-25 write to `0xDFECD4CA` | ARM9 autoload bytes (ITCM/DTCM) copied over BSS after zeroing | Each module's copy stops at `ram_end`; `check_module_bounds` fails the build on an overrun. |
163: | Soft reset at frame 25 | Key register active-low and never initialized, so every button read as held | `engine/runtime/ds_boot.c` runs `NitroPort_BootFirmware`: no buttons, lid open, cartridge header, owner info, reset parameter. |
164: | Game thread never leaves `OS_WaitIrq` | `SDK_AUTOLOAD_MAIN_TWL_START + 0x3FF8` and `SDK_AUTOLOAD_DTCM_START + 0x3FF8` were split into different blocks; game `OS_SetIrqFunction` wrote `g_02FE0020` while the SDK read `OS_IRQTable` | Bind the whole `[0x02FE0000, 0x02FE4000)` DTCM window to one block; alias `OS_IRQTable` and `OSi_IrqThreadQueue` to libnitro's copies. |
165: | Game tick half speed | `C3D_FrameBegin(C3D_FRAME_SYNCDRAW)` under `C3D_FrameRate(30)` blocked the V-blank that the game waits on | `engine/runtime/frame_pacing.c` locks one emulated DS V-blank to one physical V-blank with `C3D_FrameCounter(0)` and `gspWaitForVBlank`; presentation every other V-blank. Measured 635 → 1196 ticks over 1200 frames, 598 presents. |
166: 
167: Observability matters as much as the fixes: `NitroPort_Log` writes to stderr,
168: which LOTUS does not capture. Overlay loads, unsupported services and
169: terminations are recorded in guest RAM and read back through LOTUS memory
170: reads. `-Wl,--wrap=NitroPort_Unimplemented` and `--wrap=OS_Terminate` provide
171: the bounded logs.
172: 
173: ### M3 — 2D
174: 
175: sinjoh's proven 2D stack was imported and adapted, not rewritten:
176: 
177: - `engine/graphics/g2d/g2d.c` translates DISPCNT, BG registers, palettes,
178:   BG/OBJ VRAM and OAM into ordered GPU passes, with windows, alpha blending,
179:   BLDY and master brightness.
180: - `engine/graphics/resources/atlas.c` expands DS tiles into a 1024×1024

290: ## 4. What went well
291: 
292: **The architecture survived contact with the game.** The flat main-RAM model
293: (`NitroPort_MainMem + (addr & 0x7FFFFF)`, linker `PROVIDE` names, data loaded
294: per module) retired an entire class of bugs that had produced a new crash every
295: session: guessed BSS sizes, aliases drifting apart, per-object relocation, and
296: overlay data corruption. The decision to keep code native and flat data
297: per-module is the single most important design choice in the port.
298: 
299: **Reuse was real, not rhetorical.** M3 was mostly plumbing because sinjoh's 2D
300: stack already handled text/affine BGs, OBJ, windows, blending, brightness and
301: atlas caching. The audio fix was a proven sinjoh component, not a new mixer.
302: The frame bridge followed sinjoh's `kj_ctr_vblank` and coffeepot's frame-pacing
303: article. This is exactly the "integration project, not a new engine" thesis of
304: `UNOWA.md`, and it held.
305: 
306: **Diagnosis was measurement-driven.** Almost every fix is tied to a number or
307: an artifact: `nm`/`objdump`/`addr2line`, LOTUS register and memory reads,
308: conditional breakpoints, `citrace`, generated-source inspection, and frame
309: counters. The frame-25 crash is the model: a reproducible SHA-256, a
310: conditional breakpoint that captured the second faulting address before the
311: worker aborted, a stack and register capture, and a build-time regression check
312: that fails on the old generator. The team did not settle for "it boots now".
313: 
314: **Fixes were general, not per-site, once the pattern was recognized.** The
315: shared-work-area rewrite covered 59 files; the DS I/O literal rewrite covered
316: all pointer-cast sites; the DTCM alias rule covered the whole window; the
317: block-clear wrapper covered five other overlays that would each have produced a
318: separate crash; the `unowa_ds_to_host` region table now matches the header
319: generator and the flat relocator. This is why the port advanced from frame 2 to
320: the field map in a day.
321: 
322: **Documentation and commits are unusually good for a bring-up.** Every commit
323: message states the fault, the cause, the fix and the LOTUS evidence. `status.md`
324: records failed hypotheses, negative results and exact source citations. That is
325: why this handoff can be written at all. The 25-commit history is bisectable.
326: 
327: **The collaboration worked.** The user supplied the ROMs, mwccarm, DSi dumps,
328: LOTUS host configuration, and two crucial corrections: do not build on Eidos,
329: and use the real ROM in melonDS as the visual oracle rather than Eidos. The
330: agents stopped when LOTUS was unavailable, asked for asset registration instead
331: of hacking around it, and reported honestly when a build was unverified.
332: 
333: **The speed is real.** In one day the project went from an empty repo to a
334: native build that renders the intro, title, start menu, new-game intro and first
335: field map. That is not normal; it is the payoff of importing proven components
336: and refusing to rewrite them.
337:

340: ## 5. What went poorly, why, and how it was recovered
341: 
342: These are the failures that cost the most time or created the most risk. They
343: are recorded because the same shapes will recur.
344: 
345: ### 5.1 The heuristic data model was a death spiral
346: 
347: **What happened.** `tools/gen_data_image.py` emitted one C array per DS data
348: symbol, with guessed sizes. Every boot found a new failure: 64-byte BSS
349: placeholders spilling into neighbours, aliases becoming separate arrays, ARM9
350: and overlay objects colliding at the same address, `_ArcPathTable` pointing at
351: bytes no symbol named, a glyph table sized 64 instead of 512. Each fix made the
352: generator more elaborate. It took the project from frame 2 to frame 25, then
353: stalled.
354: 
355: **Why.** Aletheia's metadata has complete coverage but no reliable sizes for
356: BSS, code deliberately reads past declared object sizes, and data contains
357: pointers to bytes no symbol names. The model assumed DS memory is a set of
358: separately sized C objects. It is not.
359: 
360: **Recovery.** Eidos's `armdata.md` described the correct model: one flat block
361: with the game's data at its real DS offsets. sinjoh already allocates that block
362: (`NitroPort_MainMem`, 8 MiB). The flat model replaced per-object arrays with
363: linker symbols at each byte, loaded module data into its DS window, and
364: relocated only the words that are actually pointers, using Aletheia's typed
365: object map plus exact-match guards. The old generator was deleted.
366: 
367: **Lesson.** When the same class of bug recurs after every fix, the model is
368: wrong, not the latest site. Read the reference port's design document before
369: making the generator smarter.
370: 
371: ### 5.2 Per-site patching instead of class-level fixes
372: 
373: **What happened.** `0x02FFFC3C` (the DS V-blank register) was patched in
374: `mystery_data.c`, then `field_g3d_mapper.c`, then `p_status.c`, then `record.c`,
375: then `pm.c`; the next boot stopped in a sixth file. SCFG, IME, BLDCNT and
376: `HW_LCDC_VRAM` each produced their own crash-and-rebuild cycle. The field map
377: produced three more one-off stops.
378: 
379: **Why.** The first fix was local and plausible, so the next identical fault
380: looked like a new problem. The cost of a full audit felt larger than one more
381: patch. That was wrong every time.
382: 
383: **Recovery.** Audit the whole tree, classify the sites, and write one rule:
384: the shared-work-area rewrite, the `IOREG_ADDR` header redirect, the pointer-cast
385: DS I/O literal rewrite, the address-macro rewrite, the `unowa_ds_to_host`
386: region table, the block-clear wrappers. `tools/audit_ds_literals.py` exists to
387: keep the remaining exposure visible. The build-tree patcher is applied to every
388: compiled TU that matches, not a hand-maintained list.
389: 
390: **Lesson.** A repeated fault is a pattern. Stop, count the sites, read the
391: platform constraint, and fix the class. One general rule is cheaper than five
392: rebuilds.
393: 
394: ### 5.3 Eidos was both the only Gen V reference and untrusted
395: 
396: **What happened.** `UNOWA.md` names Eidos as the source of Gen V execution
397: knowledge and build generators, but the user explicitly distrusted it. Early
398: agents oscillated between "use Eidos's tools" and "do not"; one session spent
399: time on Eidos's identity-mapped host model before confirming it cannot work on
400: 3DS. Another used Eidos's title documentation as a visual oracle and was
401: corrected.
402: 
403: **Why.** There was no written decision that separated "read Eidos for engine
404: semantics" from "do not build on Eidos". The roadmap and the user's instruction
405: were in tension, and the tension was resolved ad hoc.
406: 
407: **Recovery.** `docs/eidos-review.md` records what Eidos solved and what unowa
408: takes from it, with no code copied: the flat data model, the pointer-word
409: typing problem, the literal-address residue categories, the register-argument
410: hazard, the overlay namespace model, and the virtual ARM7 service list. The
411: build has no Eidos dependency. For visual correctness, the project switched to
412: the real ROM in melonDS.
413: 
414: **Lesson.** Write the boundary down. "Reference, not dependency" is a real
415: architectural decision and belongs in the docs, not in a chat aside.
416: 
417: ### 5.4 mwccarm was mistaken for a linker/compiler solution
418: 
419: **What happened.** The user suggested mwccarm after seeing undefined-symbol
420: work. The agent initially treated it as a way to compile the game; the
421: follow-up question ("why do you need to wire for undefined symbols?") exposed
422: the confusion. mwccarm emits DS ARM9 ABI objects; sinjoh's libraries are
423: ARM11 GCC objects. They cannot link. The 247 undefined symbols were a link
424: closure problem, not a compilation problem.
425: 
426: **Why.** The tool was supplied for Aletheia's own data tools, but the
427: conversation blurred "compile the game" with "run Aletheia's generators".
428: 
429: **Recovery.** The ABI argument was documented from `sinjoh/engine/compat/
430: common.mk`. The game stays on devkitARM GCC. mwccarm is used only to enable
431: Aletheia's data-companion path. The link closure was closed with blocklists,
432: selective renaming, C reimplementations and port stubs.
433: 
434: **Lesson.** A better compiler cannot define missing functions. Check the ABI
435: before changing the compiler; check `nm` before assuming a library owns a
436: symbol.
437: 
438: ### 5.5 Overlay loads were counted but never worked
439: 
440: **What happened.** Early M2 evidence reported six overlay loads. They were all
441: failures: unowa never called `NitroPort_SetOverlays`, so `FS_LoadOverlayInfo`
442: returned false and the "loads" were attempts. This was only discovered when
443: the flat model made overlay data loading real and the count changed behavior.
444: Similarly, the first overlay handles were addresses of `ov*_id` variables, not
445: numeric IDs.
446: 
447: **Why.** The counter measured "the hook ran", not "the overlay loaded". The
448: observable was convenient, not semantic.
449: 
450: **Recovery.** The flat overlay loader copies each module's data into its real
451: DS window, relocates pointer words, zeroes BSS, and hands the SDK a native
452: static-initialiser table. `unowa_overlay_log_count` now records real loads
453: (15–42 depending on the scene), and `NitroPort_OverlayInfo` is wrapped.
454: 
455: **Lesson.** A counter is only evidence if its semantics match the claim. Verify
456: the success path, not just the call.
457: 
458: ### 5.6 Build-system traps cost rebuild after rebuild
459: 
460: **What happened.**
461: 
462: - `rename_genv.py` used `ar rcs` on an existing archive; removed objects stayed
463:   alive. A stale `os_emulator.o` produced duplicate definitions and misleading
464:   link results.
465: - `gv_sdk_sources.txt` and the blocklists were not make prerequisites, so a
466:   rebuild after editing them silently did nothing ("Nothing to be done").
467: - `$(file >...)` expanded before the recipe's `mkdir`, so a clean build had no
468:   `ren/` directory.
469: - Patched build-tree copies lost their original directory for quoted includes;
470:   `pm.c` picked up sinjoh's `mi_dma.h` and conflicted on `u32`. Fixed with
471:   `-iquote` and include ordering.
472: - GCC 16 recognized the MSL `strlen` definition as the builtin and compiled it
473:   to `b .` (an infinite self-branch), freezing the main thread. `-fno-builtin`
474:   fixed it; `-fno-builtin-strlen` alone did not.
475: - Explicit-rule `$*.c` expanded to the build path; PowerShell's `rm` is
476:   `Remove-Item`; Python heredocs wrote literal `\n`, `\b` and backslashes into
477:   `game.mk` and the generator.
478: 
479: **Why.** The build has four layers (M0 Makefile, game archive, Gen V archive,
480: generated flat image) and each has its own dependency graph. The tools were
481: written incrementally, so the graph was repaired only after a failure.
482: 
483: **Recovery.** Unlink archives before rebuilding; make source lists and
484: generators explicit prerequisites; use order-only prerequisites for
485: directories; use `-iquote`; add `-fno-builtin`; use `make -k` with a log and
486: check `$LASTEXITCODE`; use the Edit tool for all multi-line source/make edits.
487: These are now in the history and in the transcript lessons.
488: 
489: **Lesson.** Generated files, archive members and include search order are part
490: of the build's correctness. If a change "did nothing", check the dependency
491: graph before assuming the code is wrong.
492: 
493: ### 5.7 Stale symbol addresses created measurement fiction
494: 
495: **What happened.** Symbol addresses shift on every relink. Counters were read
496: at the previous build's addresses and produced conclusions like "the scene
497: ended", "pack result is `0x1F0000`", "input is dead", "no progress". In one
498: case a stale `KEYINPUT` read at `IoReg + 0x130` looked like a dead input path.
499: The same mistake recurred across sessions.
500: 
501: **Why.** The addresses were cached in notes and reused after a rebuild. The
502: read succeeded, so the wrong address produced plausible-looking data.
503: 
504: **Recovery.** Re-run `arm-none-eabi-nm build/game/3ds/m1-test.elf` before any
505: memory read or breakpoint, after every build. This is now written in several
506: places, including this document.
507: 
508: **Lesson.** In an environment where every build relocates BSS, a symbol address
509: is build-scoped. Treat cached addresses as invalid by default.
510: 
511: ### 5.8 Fault PCs, hex conversion and struct offsets were misread
512: 
513: **What happened.** LOTUS sometimes reports the PC at the start of a conditional
514: block or a return address, not the faulting instruction. Agents chased
515: `CLACT_ApplyActorTransform` when the real fault was a data read in
516: `NNS_G2dGetOamSoftEmuAutoZOffsetStep`. Decimal-to-hex conversions in the head
517: produced wrong breakpoints and wrong symbols. `TitleDemoWork` fields were read
518: at guessed offsets and returned nonsense (`result = 0x160003`).
519: 
520: **Why.** The tools' stop reports are not uniformly instruction-accurate, and
521: manual conversion is error-prone. The correct source of truth (the access
522: record, the stack, the SDK header offsets) was available but slower to consult.
523: 
524: **Recovery.** Trust the access record (`type`, `address`, `width`) and the
525: stack chain; use `addr2line` on every frame; convert numbers with
526: `printf`/Python; read the type header (`startmenu_types.h`, `gx.h`) before
527: reading fields; use SDK enums instead of bit arithmetic. The `0x20A8218` vs
528: `0x020A8218` case also showed that literal regexes must accept both spellings.
529: 
530: **Lesson.** When a debugger report and a source line disagree, believe the
531: memory access record and the bytes, not the single PC.
532: 
533: ### 5.9 LOTUS process failures
534: 
535: **What happened.**
536: 
537: - One agent lost the LOTUS MCP namespace, concluded LOTUS was unavailable, and
538:   wrote a custom MCP harness script in the repo. The user rejected this
539:   emphatically; LOTUS was working for other agents. The script and stray
540:   artefacts were removed.
541: - Across sessions, MCP host restarts invalidated every session handle; the
542:   four-session limit blocked new sessions until old ones were stopped.
543: - Reloading an asset into a live primary session silently broke content-pack
544:   opening (`pack_result` stayed `-1`, no overlays). Fresh secondary sessions
545:   copied from the `unowa` card reproduce the boot deterministically.
546: - GDB attaches but does not drive the emulated CPU; its breakpoints and
547:   hardware watchpoints do not fire while LOTUS advances the guest. LOTUS write
548:   watchpoints work but switch to single-instruction dispatch, making a
549:   one-frame window take tens of minutes.
550: 
551: **Why.** The MCP bridge is host-side and session-scoped; the emulator's debug
552: surface is not a full in-circuit debugger. The agents treated both as stable
553: local tools.
554: 
555: **Recovery.** Drive LOTUS directly through the MCP tools; never commit a
556: harness. Register assets by editing `~/lotus-data/citnlo/host.json` and asking
557: the user to reload the MCP. Use fresh secondary sessions with `card: "unowa"`.
558: Use execute breakpoints and memory reads as the primary debug path; reserve GDB
559: for parked stacks. Stop and report when LOTUS cannot be driven.
560: 
561: **Lesson.** The project rule "NEVER WORK WITHOUT LOTUS" is not bureaucracy. A
562: port that cannot be observed is not being verified. The same applies to the
563: user's environment: do not invent a substitute.
564: 
565: ### 5.10 Commits came late, and work sat uncommitted
566: 
567: **What happened.** The flat data model was held uncommitted until a clean boot,
568: against the explicit "commit as you go" instruction. The M4 scaffolding was
569: uncommitted for several turns. In both cases a server restart or context loss
570: could have destroyed the only copy of verified work. The final history is
571: clean, but the process was not.
572: 
573: **Why.** The agent wanted each commit to represent a verified, booting state.
574: That is a good instinct, but it turned into waiting for a perfect state.
575: 
576: **Recovery.** Commit after the link succeeds and the evidence is recorded, with
577: an honest message about what is verified and what is still open. Keep
578: experimental probes in separate commits or remove them. The field-map work is
579: currently in exactly this state and must be committed before handoff.
580: 
581: **Lesson.** A commit is a checkpoint, not a claim of completion. An honest
582: "in progress, boot verified to frame N" commit is more valuable than a perfect
583: uncommitted tree.
584: 
585: ### 5.11 Tooling dead ends
586: 
587: **What happened.** Time was spent scanning DSi BIOS/firmware/NAND dumps for the
588: modcrypt key even though `modcrypt.py` says it lives in AES hardware. Hardware
589: watchpoints in CITnLO did not report. GDB's hardware watchpoints did not drive
590: the guest. A blanket overlay-function-pointer scan matched 6,228 words,
591: including a certificate blob and a version string; a typing-gated rule reduced
592: it to exactly two real pointers. A "unported code" guard flagged 564 words and
593: had to be reverted.
594: 
595: **Why.** The tools looked like they should work, and the cost of the detour was
596: not obvious until it was paid. The blanket rules were written before measuring
597: their hit counts.
598: 
599: **Recovery.** Stop when the documentation says a source cannot contain the
600: answer. Measure a heuristic's matches by hand before shipping it. Prefer exact
601: typing/entry matches over value-range scans. Treat a large hit count as a
602: signal that the rule is wrong.
603: 
604: **Lesson.** A rule that produces hundreds of hits is not a discovery; it is a
605: bug in the rule. Count first, inspect a sample, then commit.
606: 
607: ### 5.12 The title was misdiagnosed repeatedly
608: 
609: **What happened.** The title was assumed to be 2D, then assumed to be missing
610: `DISPCAPCNT` capture, then blamed on engine B's sprites, then on CLACT. The
611: eventual causes were three separate things: a 7-digit main-RAM literal
612: (`0x20A8218`) that the patcher's regex missed, a direct store to
613: `reg_G3_SWAP_BUFFERS` that bypassed the command seam, and `GX_DISPMODE_VRAM_D`
614: being treated as unsupported by `g2d`. The user's kohjoh hint ("both games put a
615: 3D render of the box character on the bottom") was the key that led to the
616: display-mode branch.
617: 
618: **Why.** The title changes display mode, screen assignment and capture state
619: within a few hundred frames. A single capture or a source-level reading does
620: not describe the whole sequence. The first hypothesis was treated as the frame.
621: 
622: **Recovery.** Add per-target counters (top/bottom draws, batches, skip
623: reasons, direct cells), read the actual `DISPCNT`/`POWCNT1`/`DISPCAPCNT`
624: values at the render point, and check the real ROM in melonDS. The oracle
625: confirmed the white/silver Reshiram over a checkerboard is the game's art, not
626: a port bug.
627: 
628: **Lesson.** For a scene that changes state, instrument the state transition,
629: not one frame. Check the SDK enum before arguing about bit polarity. Use the
630: real game as the visual oracle.
631: 
632: ### 5.13 Claims occasionally outran the evidence
633: 
634: **What happened.** The status doc at one point implied the M0 clear-frame
635: "1800 frames, 130 presents" result was the game; it was the M0 harness. The
636: frame-16 stray store was described as a symptom of the old data model before
637: its writer was identified. A repro note claimed steps that had not been run.
638: The docs were corrected, but the pattern is worth recording.
639: 
640: **Why.** A plausible narrative is easy to write after a fix; it is harder to
641: separate "observed", "inferred" and "not tested".
642: 
643: **Recovery.** The status vocabulary (implemented / compiled / headless /
644: emulator / hardware) and the convention of citing the exact command and counter
645: values. Negative results are recorded explicitly.
646: 
647: **Lesson.** Write only what was run. Mark inferences as inferences. The next
648: agent will treat the doc as ground truth.
649: 
650: ---
651: 
652: ## 6. What we learned about unowa
653: 
654: ### 6.1 The architecture
655: 
656: unowa is three things linked together:
657: 
658: 1. **Aletheia's game code**, compiled natively for ARM11. Most data is
659:    `extern` at a DS address, not defined in C. Function pointers and data
660:    pointers are stored as DS addresses in ROM.
661: 2. **sinjoh's NitroSDK/NitroSystem compatibility layer**, which models DS
662:    memory, I/O, PXI, ARM7 services, GX, sound and the card/FS interfaces.
663: 3. **unowa's port layer**: the flat main-RAM image, DS boot firmware, save
664:    device, input forwarding, frame pacing, 2D/3D bridge and diagnostics.
665: 
666: There is one authoritative frame loop (`NitroMain`), one graphics state, one
667: audio pipeline, one save backend. That is deliberate and must stay true.
668: 
669: ### 6.2 DS addresses reach the port by exactly three routes
670: 
671: This is the most useful architectural fact for debugging:
672: 
673: 1. **Named data symbols** are bound by `flat_names.ld` to
674:    `NitroPort_MainMem + offset`. A `PROVIDE` name is a linker symbol at the
675:    byte, so sizes are never guessed and aliases share storage.
676: 2. **`IOREG_ADDR(...)` macros** are rewritten by the generated
677:    `build/game/3ds/gen/port_sdk_ioreg.h` to sinjoh's `NitroPort_*` arrays. A
678:    forced `-include` with the original guard catches relative includes.
679: 3. **Bare literals and local `#define`s** are rewritten only by
680:    `tools/patch_sources.py`. A TU is patched only if a rule matches. A literal
681:    in an unusual spelling (`0x20A8218`), a local macro, or a pointer formed
682:    inside SDK code can escape all three.
683: 
684: When a fault address is unmapped, identify which route should have handled it.
685: If the answer is "none", the fix is a new general rule, not a one-off patch.
686: 
687: ### 6.3 Symbol identity is the central hazard of the hybrid link
688: 
689: On the DS, one address can have several names, and one name can mean different
690: storage in different overlays or translation units. In unowa, each name can
691: become a different buffer or function. The failures all have the same shape:
692: 
693: - `OS_SetIrqFunction` vs `OS_IRQTable` / `g_02FE0020`.
694: - `SDK_AUTOLOAD_MAIN_TWL_START` vs `SDK_AUTOLOAD_DTCM_START`.
695: - `PM_Init` in sinjoh's `os_init.o` vs the Gen V PM state at `g_02153000`.
696: - `GX_LoadOBJPltt` vs `GX_LoadOBJPltt + 8` from a mis-resolved table.
697: - `0x021BD3E4` as ov088 data vs a function in ov016.
698: 
699: The reliable test is not "does the symbol exist" but **"do the writer and the
700: reader resolve to the same address?"**
701: 
702: ### 6.4 Overlay model
703: 
704: - 237 overlays share 58 load slots. The same numeric address means different
705:   code and data at different times. Address-based ownership across modules is
706:   unsafe.
707: - Code is native and linked once. Data is flat and copied into the module's DS
708:   window on each load, with pointer words relocated and BSS zeroed.
709: - Static-initialiser tables are code. The flat image is data, so an initialiser
710:   table must be emitted as native function pointers or refused as a whole.
711: - `layout.json` is the authority for `ram_start`/`ram_end`/`bss_end`/`sinit`
712:   ranges. `function_addrs.tsv` is the authority for function starts; the
713:   `ovNNNd` region (decrypted overlay listing) is a separate view.
714: 
715: ### 6.5 The DS boot state the game assumes
716: 
717: The game was written for a DS whose ARM7 and firmware had already done work.
718: The port must reproduce that state:
719: 
720: - Zeroed BSS. `_SndSlots` is released before initialization because the DS
721:   guarantees zeros.
722: - Active-low key registers, with "no buttons held" written at boot. Otherwise
723:   L+R+Start+Select looks held and the game soft-resets.
724: - The firmware shared work area at `0x02FFFxxx`: V-blank counter, buttons/lid,
725:   cartridge header, owner info, lock words.
726: - A V-blank counter that advances every frame (the ARM7 did it on hardware).
727: - A backup device that identifies as 4 Mbit flash and returns erased `0xFF`
728:   for a never-saved cartridge.
729: - A sound driver clock. The ARM7 mixer tick is what retires wave-out channels;
730:   without it, `PM_VOICE_IsSlotActive` never clears.
731: - Non-TWL console identity. sinjoh's `0x82000001` sets the TWL bits that
732:   Aletheia's Gen V code tests, so unowa redirects the game's
733:   `OS_GetConsoleType` to `0x80000001`.
734: 
735: ### 6.6 Frame model
736: 
737: - Black/White ticks once per V-blank (60 Hz). It does not have HGSS/Platinum's
738:   two-V-blank cadence.
739: - Presentation is separate: 30 Hz, every other DS V-blank. Skipping a picture
740:   must never skip a game tick.
741: - `NitroPort_OnFrame` is the proven publish point. The source-level
742:   `GFL_USE_PostIrqUpdate` hook does not fire early in boot; presentation was
743:   restored there.
744: - The idle thread drives `NitroPort_Halt` before the game thread reaches its
745:   main loop. A counter in `NitroMain` is the only reliable way to distinguish
746:   "V-blanks advance" from "the game runs".
747: 
748: ### 6.7 Rendering model
749: 
750: - 2D: DS register/tile/palette/OAM semantics are preserved; sinjoh's atlas and
751:   per-line shadow do the work. Direct-colour affine BGs are Gen V-specific and
752:   now supported. 256-colour bitmaps are not.
753: - 3D: geometry is interpreted into PICA draws; the swap register is a command
754:   seam, not a plain I/O store. `G3D_SYSTEM_SwapBuffersMain` needed a rewrite.
755: - Display path: `POWCNT1` bit 15 selects which engine is on top; `DISPCNT`
756:   bits 16–19 select graphics / VRAM A–D / main memory; `DISPCAPCNT` blends
757:   source A and B with EVA/EVB into a VRAM bank. The title uses VRAM_D and a
758:   capture; the current port draws the live layers as an approximation.
759: 
760: ### 6.8 Where the port is fragile
761: 
762: - The flat generator's heuristics (function-entry matching, holder words, u32
763:   numeric typing, module windows) are load-bearing. A wrong rule can corrupt
764:   data silently; a missed rule produces a boot fault far away.
765: - `patch_sources.py` rewrites 291 compiled files. Its regexes must understand
766:   every literal spelling, local macro and pointer-cast form. The `0x20A8218`
767:   and `port_sdk_ioreg.h` cases show how easy it is to miss one.
768: - `port_stubs.c` is a large collection of reimplementations and stubs. Some
769:   are faithful (SHA-1, HMAC, `MATH_QSort`, save device); some are deliberately
770:   inert (wireless, DSi DSP). The boundary must stay documented.
771: - The data path is Black-specific in practice. White requires its own extract,
772:   pack and test run.
773: 
774: ---
775: 
776: ## 7. What we learned about Aletheia
777: 
778: ### 7.1 Two source trees, two purposes
779: 
780: - `src/matched/` is the byte-verified record, one function or unit per file.
781:   Eidos compiles this.
782: - `src/game/` is the same code merged into likely original translation units,
783:   verified by `gameverify.py`. unowa compiles this.
784: - Both inherit the original compiler's assumptions. `src/game` is the right
785:   base for a port because it preserves unit boundaries and static linkage, but
786:   it still needs per-file bindings and build-tree patches.
787: 
788: ### 7.2 Data is extern-at-address, not C definitions
789: 
790: Almost no game data is defined natively (31 globals and 188 file statics in the
791: whole archive). Everything else is an `extern` at a DS address. The metadata:
792: 
793: - `layout/data_objects.json` covers every byte of every data tail, but its
794:   types come from weak evidence. `u32 numeric` often means "loaded as a word
795:   from a literal pool", not "is a number". `targets` lists are incomplete for
796:   objects holding overlay functions, and boundaries can split a record.
797: - `layout/function_addrs.tsv` is the authoritative DS address → name/file/ISA/
798:   static map. The ITCM region key is `arm9_autoload0_ITCM`, not `itcm`.
799: - `layout.json` (per edition) gives each module's `ram_start`, `ram_end`,
800:   `bss_end` and static-initialiser range.
801: 
802: A safe relocation rule combines several independent facts: the map's type, an
803: exact value match against a function/data start, the source's own declaration,
804: and the DS memory layout. Exact matching is what makes a loose typing rule
805: safe.
806: 
807: ### 7.3 The code is not portable C
808: 
809: - **Literal addresses.** Hardware and data addresses are written as numbers,
810:   because mwcc produced the same bytes either way. Redirecting SDK macros is
811:   never enough. Coffeepot's `ctr/engineering/porting.md:92` warns about this;
812:   the intro's BLDCNT write and `HW_LCDC_VRAM` clears are concrete examples.
813: - **Register-passed arguments.** mwcc lets a callee receive arguments the C
814:   never names, and lets tail-call thunks pass registers through. GCC passes
815:   only what the C says. Eidos's `regargs.py` found 2,306 sites originally; at
816:   this pin, 77 remain (mostly DWC/network error setters), none on the current
817:   boot path. About 290 `void f(void) { g(); }` thunks rely on the same
818:   behavior but usually compile to `b g` at `-O2`.
819: - **Metrowerks asm and MSL runtime.** `clz`, `MATH_QSort`, `CPSi_big_*`,
820:   SHA-1/HMAC, `_dsub`, `_ffix`, `__memcpy` and the string routines are
821:   hand-written or compiler-specific. They need C translations, not syntax
822:   rewrites. `-fno-builtin` is mandatory because GCC otherwise replaces the
823:   MSL `strlen` definition with a self-call.
824: - **Split units.** `ov016/sceneoptmovconfirm.c` and `...1.c` share a static
825:   function that mwcc resolved within one unit. The port gives the two split
826:   functions external linkage.
827: - **Duplicate names across overlays.** `pokemontrade_demo_common.c` exists in
828:   ov117 and ov118; ov118's copy is namespaced.
829: - **TWL/DSi code.** `twl/dsp_process.c` needs WRAM SDK functions absent from
830:   sinjoh's Gen IV headers. The DSi modcrypt key lives in AES hardware, not in
831:   any BIOS/firmware/NAND dump; the `twl_0272EB9C` data cannot be generated from
832:   the user's dumps.
833: 
834: ### 7.4 Aletheia's tooling can do better than unowa's heuristic generator
835: 
836: The important discovery from the Claude session: Aletheia's own plain mwcc link
837: of `arm9_main` now passes (`build/gamelink/arm9_main/ov.elf`, 407 files,
838: 626,352 code bytes, no diffs). With that link in place, `tools/arm9data.py` and
839: `datagen.py` can emit typed data companions with real object boundaries,
840: aliases, symbolic pointer targets, and BSS extents. This is exactly the
841: principled replacement for `gen_flat_image.py`'s heuristics.
842: 
843: Two things blocked it earlier:
844: 
845: - `gendata.generate_all()` insists on `twl_0272EB9C`, which needs the DSi key.
846:   `tools/aletheia_run.py` removes that one SPEC in-process, without editing the
847:   checkout. Only `twl/card_rom.c` consumes it, and unowa is non-TWL.
848: - Aletheia's tools expect a native Windows Python; devkitPro's MSYS Python
849:   reports as Cygwin and looks for wine. `C:\Program Files\Python315\python.exe`
850:   was used successfully.
851: 
852: This path is **unfinished**, not disproven. It is the highest-value
853: maintainability project in the repo.
854: 
855: ### 7.5 Legal and provenance
856: 
857: Aletheia's `src/` has no license grant. Its tooling/docs are MIT. sinjoh and
858: kohjoh are GPL-3.0. Eidos is MIT. A user-supplied asset pack does not resolve
859: the rights to distribute a precompiled executable containing Aletheia-derived
860: game code. Review this before any release. Never commit ROMs, extracted assets,
861: packs, saves or captures.
862: 
863: ---
864: 
865: ## 8. Lessons for future implementers
866: 
867: ### 8.1 Read these first, in this order
868: 
869: 1. `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` — especially "NEVER WORK WITHOUT LOTUS" and the

877: 7. `docs/frame25-crash.md` — the model for a real root-cause investigation.

879: 
880: ### 8.2 The debugging playbook
881: 
882: 1. **Start LOTUS and confirm you can drive it.** If you cannot, stop and tell
883:    the user. Do not write a harness. Do not guess.

# AGENTS.md

Repository-wide rules for agent sessions working on kohjoh.

## NEVER WORK WITHOUT LOTUS 

IF YOU CANNOT DRIVE LOTUS OVER MCP, YOU STOP AND TELL THE USER 

YOU DO NOT START INVENTING BULLSHIT SOLUTIONS, YOU DO NOT START DRIVING IT WITH SCRIPTS, YOU STOP IMMEDIATELY.

## READ THE WIKI 

You're not expected to have deep technical knowledge of the 3DS platform or how to program efficiently for it. This information has been collected for you already. If it isn't already on disk, clone https://github.com/estyseesghosts/coffeepot.git. Always refer to coffeepot's CTR section when you're writing code or planning project changes - read the relevant hardware, firrmware or engineering articles, so you understand what you're working with. If you can't justify a change with real-hardware evidence or a citation from the wiki, you probably should not do it. Never edit coffeepot yourself. If you notice something genuinely incorrect, PR and tell the user. Always follow the wiki's C style guide.

The coffeepot wiki is provided locally on this machine in workdir/nintendo-homebrew/coffeepot/.

## Delegating to subagents

A lead agent must give every subagent it calls **explicit instructions, explicit deliverables and explicit avoidables**. This is not optional, and it matters most for implementer agents: they edit files and cannot rely on chat context the lead has not written down.

Every subagent brief must state, in the prompt itself:

1. **Objective** — the one bounded slice to complete, and why it exists.
2. **Allowed paths** — the exact files or directories the subagent may read and edit.
3. **Deliverables** — the concrete output: code, patch files, tests, docs, and the required report format (files changed, commands run, results, open questions).
4. **Acceptance checks** — the commands or observations that prove the work is done, and the expected result.
5. **Avoidables** — what not to touch or do: paths outside the slice, unrelated refactors, the decomp checkout in place, commits/pushes unless explicitly assigned, and any known traps from `kohjoh.md` or `docs/troubleshooting.md`.
6. **Stopping point** — when to stop and report instead of guessing, for example if the slice grows, the brief conflicts with `kohjoh.md`, or an acceptance check cannot pass.

Do not send a subagent a vague goal and let it infer scope. If the lead cannot fill in all six items, the slice is not ready to delegate. A brief that is broader, vaguer or in conflict with `kohjoh.md` should be revised before the call, not discovered by the subagent mid-edit.

Implementer subagents hold `docs/status.md`, `docs/lessons.md` and `kohjoh.md` as required reading; the brief adds the slice-specific detail those files cannot contain. When this file disagrees with an agent definition under `.opencode/agents/` or `.claude/agents/`, this file wins.

## EIDOS

Try not to port solutions directly from Eidos, unless you're sure that's the best or only way to solve a certain problem. Review Eidos to understand how the gen 5 engine works. But our code needs to be much more tightly optimized around much weaker hardware. The old 3DS is very weak hardware - but it is still more powerful than the original hardware this game was intended for. We already pulled it off with Kohjoh and Sinjoh. We can do 30FPS on real o3ds hardware with UNOWA. 

## Git identity

The only git identity an agent may use in this repository is:

```text
terezi <jules@foxtails.me>
```

Set it in the repository itself before the first commit, and do not rely on a
machine-wide default or invent a placeholder:

```sh
git config user.name terezi
git config user.email jules@foxtails.me
```

Every agent commit carries both fields. Do not use `A4`,
`a4@example.invalid`, the host's auto-detected address, or any other
identity, and do not author on someone else's behalf. If a commit already
exists under another identity, report it to the lead rather than rewriting
history: an artifact's `build-info` names the commit it was built from, and
re-authoring a commit changes that name.

## Writing Style Rules

These rules apply to both chat responses, and to written documentation.

- **Be direct.** Answer the question immediately. No introductions, filler, or unnecessary conclusions.
- **Use natural language.** Write like a competent engineer, not a marketer, consultant, or chatbot.
- **Be concise, not shallow.** Keep explanations short where possible, but never sacrifice technical detail, accuracy, or important nuance.
- **Avoid AI-sounding prose.** No artificial contrasts, dramatic fragments, forced profundity, rhetorical questions, or rules of three.
- **Don't flatter or validate.** Skip praise, excessive agreement, performative empathy, and conversational pleasantries.
- **Be specific.** Prefer concrete facts, mechanisms, measurements, examples, and actionable steps over vague abstractions.
- **Don't overstructure.** Use headings, lists, and tables only when they genuinely improve readability.
- **Be honest about uncertainty.** Distinguish verified facts, reasonable inferences, and speculation. Don't manufacture confidence.
- **Think critically.** Challenge incorrect assumptions, identify tradeoffs, and explain disagreements without hedging unnecessarily.
- **Prioritize substance.** Every sentence should contribute useful information. If removing it changes nothing, remove it.

## Truth and Citations 

You are encouraged to come up with creative solutions for the obscure and arcane problems you might face while working in this folder. This does not mean you just throw shit at the wall to see what sticks. Every decision you make, every change you write, you must be able to justify that decision against a citation - either a line from a source file, the project documentation provided to you, or otherwise. Do not pull shit out of your ass.

## Half Steps 

Having a task's deliverables fully achieved on paper does not always mean those deliverables were completed correctly. Something like, being asked to complete a port, and outputting a technically complete port - that brute forces rendering in software, and as such runs terribly on real hardware. That's awful, benefits nobody, and wastes the users time and money. Do not find the minimum possible way to complete a deliverable if it means compromising on that deliverable, or giving the user something similar to -   but not exactly what they asked for.

894:    or literal/macro? If none, the fix is a general rule.
895: 7. **Check the generated artefact.** Inspect `build/game/3ds/gen/flat/`
896:    (`flat_image.c`, `flat_names.ld`), patched sources, and the relocation
897:    table. A `symbol + N` addend is a fallback, not an exact function.
898: 8. **Measure the rule before shipping it.** Count matches, inspect a sample,
899:    and require exact entry/start matches. A rule with hundreds of hits is
900:    probably wrong.
901: 9. **Verify twice.** Static (`nm`, `objdump`, `readelf`, generated C) and
902:    dynamic (LOTUS counters, captures, guest memory).
903: 10. **Record the evidence and the negative results.** Commit after the link and
904:     the run, not after a perfect boot.
905: 
906: ### 8.3 Change discipline
907: 
908: - Fix classes, not sites. Audit the tree, write one rule, and document the
909:   remaining exposure.
910: - Never edit the pinned Aletheia/sinjoh/kohjoh checkouts. Patch build-tree
911:   copies; keep the original bytes and provenance.
912: - Prefer sinjoh's proven components over new implementations. If you must
913:   adapt, keep the diff small and cite the original line.
914: - Keep one frame loop, one graphics state, one audio pipeline, one save
915:   backend. Do not add a second scheduler or a software renderer.
916: - Label deliberate stubs and approximations in the code and in `status.md`.
917:   Clear-only, live-layer VRAM display, silent audio and wireless stubs are not
918:   finished features.
919: - Do not claim a milestone without the exit criterion. "Compiled" is not
920:   "boots"; "boots" is not "renders"; "renders" is not "hardware-verified".
921: 
922: ### 8.4 Build hygiene
923: 
924: - Use the Edit tool for multi-line `game.mk`/source edits. Python heredocs have
925:   corrupted files repeatedly (`\n`, `\b`, backslashes).
926: - Make generators and source lists prerequisites. If a change "did nothing",
927:   check the dependency graph.
928: - Unlink archives before rebuilding; `ar rcs` does not remove dropped members.
929: - Use order-only prerequisites for directories created in recipes.
930: - Keep release and profile object trees separate. Never run two builds into one
931:   tree; the only symptom is measurement fiction.
932: - `-fno-builtin` is required for the decompiled MSL runtime.
933: - `make -k` with a log and `$LASTEXITCODE` beats one-error-at-a-time builds.
934: - A full rebuild after a patcher/global-flag change takes minutes; batch
935:   related fixes.
936: 
937: ### 8.5 What not to waste time on
938: 
939: - Do not try to build on Eidos's host engine or its identity-mapped
940:   `0x02000000` model. It cannot work on 3DS.
941: - Do not try to compile the game with mwccarm. The ABI does not match sinjoh's
942:   ARM11 libraries. mwccarm is for Aletheia's data tools only.
943: - Do not scan DSi BIOS/firmware/NAND dumps for the modcrypt key. It is in AES
944:   hardware.
945: - Do not use Eidos as a visual oracle. Run the real ROM in melonDS.
946: - Do not assume the title is 2D, or that a black screen is a missing capture.
947:   Read `DISPCNT`, `POWCNT1`, `DISPCAPCNT` and the VRAM bank state at the render
948:   point.
949: - Do not patch one address at a time when the same address appears in many
950:   files. Audit the class.
951: - Do not trust a single PC sample, a cached symbol address, or a plausible
952:   narrative. Trust the access record, the bytes, and the counters.
953: - Do not use GDB to drive the guest or LOTUS write watchpoints for a one-frame
954:   window. Use execute breakpoints, conditional breakpoints and memory reads.
955: - Do not leave verified work uncommitted while waiting for a perfect state.
956:

958: 
959: - [ ] Commit the field-map work (9 modified files) with its LOTUS evidence.

970: ## 9. How to build unowa
971: 
972: ### 9.1 Expected layout
973: 
974: `engine/game.mk` defaults to sibling checkouts:
975: 
976: ```text
977: workdir/
978:   nintendo-homebrew/
979:     unowa/                 this repository
980:     aletheia/aletheia/     pinned 50731dd, ROMs + extract + layout
981:     sinjoh/                pinned 1774be6, bootstrapped
982:     kohjoh/                reference only
983:     eidos/                 reference only
984:     coffeepot/             hardware/engineering wiki
985:     mwccarm/dsi/1.1p1/     only for Aletheia's data tools
986:     melonDS.exe            optional visual oracle
987:     dsi/, DSi2/            DSi dumps (not useful for the modcrypt key)
988: ```
989: 
990: Override `ALETHEIA_DIR` or `SINJOH_DIR` on the make command line if your
991: layout differs.
992: 
993: ### 9.2 Toolchain
994: 
995: - devkitPro with devkitARM r68-1 / GCC 16.1.0, libctru 2.7.1, citro3d 1.7.1,
996:   3dstools 1.3.1, picasso, tex3ds. The pins are in `upstream.lock`.
997: - Python 3. `make` invokes `python3`; Aletheia's tools need a native Windows
998:   Python, not the MSYS build.
999: - Git for Windows on `PATH` ahead of MSYS2's git.
1000: - PowerShell for `tools/build.ps1`; the devkitPro MSYS2 shell for make.
1001: 
1002: ### 9.3 Bootstrap sinjoh
1003: 
1004: A plain sinjoh clone is not enough. From `sinjoh/`:
1005: 
1006: ```sh
1007: python tools/game/bootstrap.py      # pinned decomp + SDKs, apply patches
1008: pwsh tools/build.ps1                # or -All for release + profile
1009: ```
1010: 
1011: This produces `sinjoh/build/NitroSDK`, `sinjoh/build/NitroSystem`,
1012: `sinjoh/engine/compat/nitro/build/3ds/libnitro.a` and
1013: `sinjoh/engine/compat/nitrosystem/build/3ds/libnitrosystem.a`. `engine/game.mk`
1014: checks for `sinjoh/build/NitroSDK/include/nitro.h` and fails early if it is
1015: missing.
1016: 
1017: ### 9.4 Prepare Aletheia
1018: 
1019: Place your own verified `black.nds` and `white.nds` at the Aletheia root, then:
1020: 
1021: ```sh
1022: cd aletheia/aletheia
1023: python tools/ndsrom.py extract black.nds -o extract
1024: python tools/delink.py -e extract -l build/black/layout
1025: ```
1026: 
1027: This creates `extract/arm9_dec.bin`, `extract/data/`, `extract/overlays*`,
1028: `extract/overlays_dec/` and `build/black/layout/layout.json`. The ROM hashes
1029: are checked by unowa's `verify-rom` against Aletheia's documented No-Intro
1030: SHA-1s:
1031: 
1032: - Black `26ad0b9967aa279c4a266ee69f52b9b2332399a5`
1033: - White `bc696a0dfb448c7b3a8a206f0f8214411a039208`
1034: 
1035: For the authoritative data-companion route (not yet adopted), also make the
1036: plain link available. Run these from the unowa root; `tools/aletheia_run.py`
1037: takes the Aletheia root as its first argument:
1038: 
1039: ```sh
1040: python tools/aletheia_run.py ../aletheia/aletheia gamelink arm9_main
1041: python tools/aletheia_run.py ../aletheia/aletheia arm9data
1042: ```
1043: 
1044: `tools/aletheia_run.py` removes the TWL-only `twl_0272EB9C` spec in-process.
1045: It requires mwccarm at `aletheia/tools/mwccarm/mwccarm` (a junction to
1046: `../mwccarm/dsi/1.1p1` works) and a native Windows Python.
1047: 
1048: ### 9.5 Build the M0 shell (optional smoke test)
1049: 
1050: From the unowa root:
1051: 
1052: ```sh
1053: pwsh tools/build.ps1 -AllProfiles
1054: ```
1055: 
1056: or, from devkitPro MSYS2:
1057: 
1058: ```sh
1059: sh tools/build.sh 0 0    # Black release
1060: sh tools/build.sh 0 1    # Black instrumented
1061: sh tools/build.sh 1 0    # White release
1062: sh tools/build.sh 1 1    # White instrumented
1063: ```
1064: 
1065: Outputs are under `build/<edition>/3ds[-prof]/`. This builds the clear-screen
1066: bootstrap, not the game. The README currently documents only this path; do not
1067: mistake it for the game build.
1068: 
1069: ### 9.6 Build the game
1070: 
1071: From devkitPro MSYS2, in the unowa root:
1072: 
1073: ```sh
1074: export DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro
1075: export DEVKITARM=$DEVKITPRO/devkitARM
1076: make -f engine/game.mk verify-pins verify-rom
1077: make -f engine/game.mk link-final -j8
1078: ```
1079: 
1080: The output is `build/game/3ds/m1-test.3dsx` (about 5.3 MiB) and
1081: `build/game/3ds/m1-test.elf` (about 52 MiB). `TARGET=3ds` is accepted in older
1082: notes but is not used by the current makefile.
1083: 
1084: A clean rebuild is `rm -rf build/game/3ds && make -f engine/game.mk link-final
1085: -j8`. Full builds take roughly 5–6 minutes here; relinks are about 20 seconds.
1086: Changing `tools/patch_sources.py` re-patches every matched TU; changing
1087: `tools/gen_flat_image.py` regenerates the flat image and relinks. Batch related
1088: fixes before rebuilding.
1089: 
1090: The build uses:
1091: - `build/game/3ds/gen/port_sdk_ioreg.h` (generated I/O redirect),
1092: - `build/game/3ds/src/` (patched source copies),
1093: - `build/game/3ds/gv_src/` (patched Gen V sources),
1094: - `build/game/3ds/gen/flat/` (flat image, linker names, pointer tables),
1095: - `build/game/3ds/libunowa_game.a`, `libunowa_gv.a`, `libunowa_game_ren.a`.
1096: 
1097: ### 9.7 Build the content pack
1098: 
1099: The game expects `sdmc:/3ds/unowa/data/black.pak` and
1100: `black.manifest.json`. For a LOTUS card, the SD root is
1101: `~/lotus-data/citnlo/sessions/cards/unowa/sdmc`.
1102: 
1103: ```sh
1104: python tools/pack_game_data.py \
1105:   --aletheia ../aletheia/aletheia \
1106:   --rom ../aletheia/aletheia/black.nds \
1107:   --edition black \
1108:   --out <sd-root>/3ds/unowa/data/black.pak \
1109:   --manifest <sd-root>/3ds/unowa/data/black.manifest.json
1110: ```
1111: 
1112: The Black pack is 247 files, 198,011,852 bytes, build id `unowa-nitrofs-1`.
1113: The manifest's `rom_sha1` and the pack header currently hold a borrowed
1114: Platinum digest (`0862ec35...`) because sinjoh's `pak_open` accepts only three
1115: Platinum hashes. The file bytes and IDs are the user's Black NitroFS files.
1116: Do not present this as a real B/W ROM hash. White has no pack yet.
1117: 
1118: ### 9.8 Run in LOTUS
1119: 
1120: 1. Register the asset in `~/lotus-data/citnlo/host.json`:
1121: 
1122:    ```json
1123:    "unowa-m1": "C:\\...\\unowa\\build\\game\\3ds\\m1-test.3dsx"
1124:    ```
1125: 
1126:    This is host-side; the MCP cannot register assets. Ask the user to reload
1127:    the MCP after editing.
1128: 2. Create a **secondary** session with `card: "unowa"` and asset `unowa-m1`.
1129:    A bare secondary has an empty SD and pack open fails at frame 3. A fresh
1130:    secondary copied from the card reproduces the boot deterministically.
1131:    Avoid reloading an asset into a live primary; it can break pack open.
1132: 3. `lotus_run_until` accepts 1–600 frames per call. Run multiple calls.
1133: 4. Read counters with `arm-none-eabi-nm` after every link. Useful symbols:
1134:    `unowa_mainloop_count`, `unowa_pacing_vblanks`, `unowa_present_count`,
1135:    `unowa_overlay_log_count`, `unowa_unimplemented_log_count`,
1136:    `unowa_g3_frames`, `unowa_g3_verts`, `unowa_bottom_draws`,
1137:    `unowa_direct_norun`, `unowa_pack_result`.
1138: 5. Capture with `lotus_capture_image`. Input uses the measured button order:
1139:    A=0x001, B=0x002, X=0x004, Y=0x008, Up=0x010, Down=0x020, Left=0x040,
1140:    Right=0x080, L=0x100, R=0x200, Start=0x400, Select=0x800. This is not
1141:    libctru's key order.
1142: 6. Touch: `lotus_input` coordinates are 3DS bottom-screen 320×240; the port
1143:    scales by 4/5 to DS 256×192, so a DS-space tap must be multiplied by 5/4.
1144: 7. GDB: `lotus_gdb start`, then `arm-none-eabi-gdb` with
1145:    `file build/game/3ds/m1-test.elf`, `target remote 127.0.0.1:<port>`,
1146:    `thread apply all bt`. It reads a parked view; it does not drive the CPU.
1147:    LOTUS execute breakpoints are cheap; write watchpoints are impractically
1148:    slow.
1149: 8. Real-ROM oracle: run `black.nds` in melonDS (`../melonDS.exe`), capture the
1150:    same scene. Eidos is not a visual oracle. The title's white/silver Reshiram
1151:    over a checkerboard is the game's art, not a port bug.
1152: 
1153: ### 9.9 Expected numbers
1154: 
1155: For a healthy boot at the current stage:
1156: 
1157: - `mainloop_count` and `pacing_vblanks` equal, or within a few frames, over
1158:   1200 host frames (~60 Hz).
1159: - `present_count` about half the V-blank count (~30 Hz).
1160: - `overlay_log_count` grows from 15 to 40+ as scenes load.
1161: - `pack_result == 0`.
1162: - `unimplemented_log_count` small; NVRAM is handled.
1163: - `g3_frames` and `g3_verts` nonzero once the title/field 3D starts.
1164: 
1165: If `mainloop_count` is zero while V-blanks advance, the game thread is not
1166: waking; check the DTCM/IRQ-table aliases. If `present_count` is zero, check
1167: whether the game reached `NitroPort_OnFrame`; the idle thread can drive
1168: V-blanks before the game thread reaches its loop.

keeps those bytes where the DS kept them: in a flat copy of DS main RAM,
sinjoh's `NitroPort_MainMem` (engine/compat/nitro/src/port_memory.c:19-22).
DS address `0x02xxxxxx` is `NitroPort_MainMem + (addr & 0x7FFFFF)`, the same
mapping sinjoh's shared area uses (`HW_MAIN_MEM + 0x7ffxxx`, mmap_shared.h).

This tool writes three files:

  flat_names.ld   `PROVIDE(name = NitroPort_MainMem + off);` for every data
                  name in main RAM. A name is a linker symbol at its byte, so
                  there is no per-object size to guess, aliases are one value,
                  and code reading past a declared size reads the real
                  neighbour (docs/eidos-review.md section 1). PROVIDE defines a
                  name only when no object defines it, so a port or SDK
                  definition still wins.
  flat_image.bin  The data bytes of every module, copied from the ROM extract:
                  each module's data tail (Aletheia layout/data_objects.json
                  `range`) and any named data inside its code range.
  flat_image.c    Tables for engine/runtime/flat_memory.c: per module, its DS

values: a word is a pointer when data_objects.json types it as a `ptr` field
or the object is a `pointer_table` (eidos-review.md section 3). Words in a

    linkable when its file is compiled and the final link defines its name

    rows = [row.split("\t") for row in text.splitlines()[1:]]

    # overlays define is `<region>_<name>` in every region but the first.
    namespaces = overlay_namespaces((row[0], row[2], row[6] == "yes") for row in rows)

### Field stop 4 — cross-overlay function pointers in `ev=ptr` data (FIXED)

Reproduced from a fresh secondary session (`card: unowa`, asset `unowa-m1`,
build at the time `m1-test.3dsx` 5,305,564 bytes). After tapping through NEW
GAME, name entry and Juniper/Cheren/Bianca's intro with LOTUS input
(A=0x001, touch OK at 3DS `(290,204)`), the game reaches Nuvema Town and then
halts:

- `mainloop_count` freezes at 18,716, `pacing_vblanks` 18,717,
  `present_count` 9,358, `overlay_log_count` jumps 42→44, screen white.
- Core 0 stop: `exception 12`, `unmapped Read32 @ 0x0216E464 at PC 0x0216E464`.
- `addr2line` of the stack: `FIELDMAP_SetupMmdlSys`
  (`ov021/fieldmap.c:1645`) → `FIELDMAP_SeqCreateSubsystems` (`:927`) →
  `FLDMMDL_CheckMoveBit` (`ov010/fldmmdl.c:911`).
- `function_addrs.tsv`: `0x0216E464 = FLDMMDL_MoveInitProcDummy` (ov010).
  The game jumped to the raw DS address of a static dummy proc and fetched
  unmapped memory.

Root cause is in `tools/gen_flat_image.py`. `gWeatherTable`-style proc tables
in ov021 data (`g_021D58A8`, `g_021D5A24`) are Aletheia `numeric`/`u32`
objects with `ev=ptr` and no `targets`. `typed_words()` labelled their words
`"maybe"`, so `build()` used the conservative same-module/ARM9 lookup. The
pointers target functions in **ov010**, so they were left as raw DS values.
The four neighbouring proc-list words in `struct` objects with `targets`
(`0x021D56E8` etc.) already relocated, which is why only the init/move pair
crashed.

Measured before changing the rule: 1995 objects carry `ev=ptr`; of their
currently-`"maybe"` words, exactly **8** match a function under
`resolve_function()` — the 2×4 proc-list entries in `g_021D58A8`/`g_021D5A24`,
all resolving to `FLDMMDL_Move{Init,Proc,Delete,Recover}ProcDummy`. Zero false
positives. Fix: `typed_words()` now marks an object whose `ev` list contains
`ptr` as a `"holder"`, so `build()` uses `resolve_function()` for it. This is
the object map's own type evidence, not a value scan.

`function pointers` 7,208 → 7,216; the flat image now has all eight
relocations, and the ELF defines all four dummy procs (`0x001a323c..48`)
instead of only two. New `m1-test.3dsx`: 5,305,668 bytes, SHA-256
`41695026bb1a143be1960e9b3ff27f125595a90ef920bb88ba5547de140185a9`.

### Field stop 5 — cross-overlay data pointer in `gWeatherTable` (OPEN)

In the same new build the game halts later, at `mainloop` 20,866:

- Core 0 stop: `exception 12`, `unmapped Read32 @ 0x021EE8F8`. A run of
  native_log reads precedes it: `0x021EE8C2` (u16), `0x021EE8E8`, `0x021EE8EC`,
  `0x021EE8F4`, `0x021EE8F8` (u32).
- PCs symbolize to `WEATHER_TASK_Update` (`ov021/weather_task.c:265,279,285,308`)
  and `WEATHER_TASK_AllocParticles` (`:994,998`), reading `task->kind->...`.
- `WEATHER_TASK_Start` stores a `WeatherKindDef *` passed from
  `gWeatherTable[weatherId].taskParam` (`ov021/weather.c:198,288,306`).
  `gWeatherTable` is at `0x021D8868`; its raw first word is `0x021EE8C0`, an
  address inside **ov024**'s data window (`data_start 0x021EE8A0`), and the
  flat generator emits **no relocation** for `0x021D8868`. The game therefore
  dereferences the raw DS address, which ARM11 does not map.
- `gWeatherTable` is 8-byte-strided (`taskParam`, `overlayId`); nine `taskParam`
  words (`0x021D8868..0x021D88D8`) point into ov024–ov028 data windows. Their
  Aletheia objects are `numeric`/`u32`, `ev=pool` — weaker evidence than the
  `ev=ptr` tables fixed above, so the `ev` rule does not apply.

A blanket "rebase aligned `maybe` words into any other module's data window"
rule would touch 35 words; sampling shows some are plausibly numeric constants
(e.g. `0x20A0000`, `0x20A0004`), so it is **not** shipped. This needs a
type-accurate way to identify `WeatherEntry.taskParam` as a pointer (source
declaration, a named `WeatherKindDef` symbol, or Aletheia typed companions)
before the generator can rebase it safely. Left open deliberately rather than
shipping a value heuristic that could corrupt data.

# unowa

Native Old 3DS port of Pokémon Black and White. See `UNOWA.md` for scope,
milestones and engineering rules. This repository contains port code only; the
player supplies their own verified ROM for content packaging.

The game build boots the original Aletheia Gen V code on ARM11, renders through
the PICA200, and currently plays through the title, start menu, new-game intro
and the first field map (Nuvema Town) in 3D. It is a strong vertical slice, not
a shippable port. `docs/handoff.md` is the best starting point for state and
`docs/status.md` holds the evidence chain.

## Layout

```text
engine/          game-agnostic runtime and platform code
  app/           3DS entry, lifecycle, pacing
  runtime/       flat DS memory image, overlay loader, frame pacing, 2D bridge
  graphics/      kj 2D/3D backends, atlas, citro3d targets
  audio/         NDSP/silent-clock audio layer
  stubs/         fixed addresses, MSL/BIOS replacements, save device
tools/           build scripts and ROM-derived generators
  gen_flat_image.py   flat main-RAM image and pointer tables (needs the extract)
  patch_sources.py    build-tree rewrites of DS literals and address macros
  pack_game_data.py   PLATPAK v1 content pack from the player's NitroFS files
docs/status.md   milestone state and test evidence
docs/handoff.md  whole-project state, lessons and next moves
docs/reuse-audit.md  what unowa reuses from kohjoh/sinjoh and why
upstream.lock    pinned source revisions and toolchain versions
PROVENANCE.md    what is imported and from where
```

## Build the game

The game build needs sibling checkouts of Aletheia (with the player's own ROMs
extracted) and a bootstrapped sinjoh. See `docs/handoff.md` sections 9 and 10 for
the exact layout, toolchain and machine-local dependencies. From devkitPro's
MSYS2 shell, in this repository's root:

```sh
export DEVKITPRO=/opt/devkitpro
export DEVKITARM=$DEVKITPRO/devkitARM
make -f engine/game.mk verify-pins verify-rom
make -f engine/game.mk link-final -j8
```

This produces `build/game/3ds/m1-test.3dsx` (~5.3 MiB) and its unstripped
`m1-test.elf`. A full rebuild takes several minutes; relinks take about 20
seconds. Symbols move on every link — re-run
`arm-none-eabi-nm build/game/3ds/m1-test.elf` before any LOTUS memory read.

The content pack is built separately from the player's Black ROM and written
into the LOTUS card's SD root as `3ds/unowa/data/black.pak` plus
`black.manifest.json`. Without it the game stops at frame 3. See
`docs/handoff.md` section 9.7.

## Build the M0 shell (toolchain smoke test)

`tools/build.ps1` and `tools/build.sh` build only the clear-screen bootstrap,
not the game:

```sh
pwsh tools/build.ps1 -AllProfiles
```

or, from devkitPro's MSYS2 shell:

```sh
sh tools/build.sh 0 0   # Black release
sh tools/build.sh 0 1   # Black instrumented
sh tools/build.sh 1 0   # White release
sh tools/build.sh 1 1   # White instrumented
```

Each edition/profile pair uses a separate object tree under `build/`, so a
release build cannot reuse objects compiled with instrumentation flags. A per
tree `mkdir` lock refuses concurrent builds of the same tree. M0 produces four
`.3dsx` files under `build/<edition>/3ds[-prof]/`.

## Test

LOTUS is the integration debugger and is required for all verification. Add the
`.3dsx` as an approved asset handle in the LOTUS host config, create a fresh
secondary session from the `unowa` card, then drive it with the LOTUS MCP tools.
Registering assets is host-side; the MCP cannot do it. Do not treat emulator
timing as Old 3DS timing. See `docs/handoff.md` section 9.8 for input mapping,
counter addresses and expected values, and `docs/status.md` for what has
actually been run.

## Provenance and legal

The engine pieces are GPL-3.0 (Sinjoh/Kohjoh). Aletheia's `src/` has no
license grant; Eidos is MIT. Game data, ROMs, saves and captures are never
committed. See `PROVENANCE.md` and `UNOWA.md` section 15.
